info.name: RideMatch API - Local Smoke Checks
info.description:
Local Postman collection for RideMatch API. Set up SQL Server first, apply Data/Migrations, set Jwt:SecretKey with .NET User Secrets, and run the API in Development. Development uses process-local in-memory Redis for single-instance interview demos; configure and start Redis for production or multi-instance runs. Base URL defaults to https://localhost:7158.

Run folders in this order: Health, Authentication, Driver Setup, Rider Ride Create/Read, Driver Ride Workflow, Rider Cancel Flow, Authorization and Validation. Use Collection Runner sequentially. The matching worker is asynchronous: after creating a ride, wait until it appears in Driver Ride History with status DriverAssigned before running the driver lifecycle requests. The sample pickup matches the driver's sample location.

Registration creates a fresh sample account each time the folder runs; its emails and tokens are stored as collection variables. This is a local development collection, not for production credentials.

item.name: 02 - Authentication

exec: pm.test("Rider registered", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201)); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.collectionVariables.set("riderToken", body.token); pm.collectionVariables.set("riderId", body.userId);
pm.test("Rider login", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.collectionVariables.set("riderToken", body.token);

pm.test("Driver registered", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201)); const body = pm.response.json(); const token = body.token || (body.data && body.data.token); pm.expect(token, "Driver registration response must include a token").to.be.a("string").and.not.empty; pm.collectionVariables.set("driverToken", token); if (pm.environment.get("driverToken") !== undefined) pm.environment.set("driverToken", token); pm.collectionVariables.set("driverUserId", body.userId || (body.data && body.data.userId));

pm.test("Driver login", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)); const body = pm.response.json(); const token = body.token || (body.data && body.data.token); pm.expect(token, "Driver login response must include a token").to.be.a("string").and.not.empty; pm.collectionVariables.set("driverToken", token); if (pm.environment.get("driverToken") !== undefined) pm.environment.set("driverToken", token);

item.description: Run this folder first. It registers and logs in a fresh rider and driver, then saves riderToken and driverToken.

item.name: 03 - Driver Setup

exec: pm.test("Driver went online", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set("driverId", body.data.driverId);

item.description: Go online and publish a fresh location before creating the sample ride.

item.name: 04 - Rider Ride Create and Read

exec: pm.test("Ride created", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201)); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.data.id).to.be.a("string"); pm.collectionVariables.set("rideId", body.data.id);

item.description: Creates a ride and stores rideId for subsequent requests.

item.name: 05 - Driver Ride Workflow

exec: pm.test("Driver can read assigned ride", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.description: Run after the matching worker assigns the sample ride to this driver. Check Driver Ride History first.

item.name: 06 - Rider Cancel Flow
item.description: Creates a second sample ride and cancels it while it is still cancellable.

item.name: 07 - Authorization and Validation

exec: pm.test("Rider cannot access driver API", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test("Driver cannot access rider API", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test("Coordinate validation rejects invalid latitude", () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

item.description: Checks expected 401/403 role responses and invalid-coordinate validation.
Hub access requires a valid bearer token. The negotiate request checks authenticated access; use a SignalR-capable client for JoinRideGroup and LeaveRideGroup WebSocket invocations.
item.name: 08 - SignalR Ride Hub

exec: pm.test("Authenticated hub negotiation", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.connectionToken).to.be.a("string");
pm.test("Unauthenticated hub negotiation is rejected", () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
